기록은 과거 시점의 상태입니다. 이후 공개 대화에서 변화가 있었다면 함께 반영하고, 과거 마음을 현재 마음으로 고정하거나 과거 이유를 소급하여 바꾸지 마세요. 선택된 기록도 현재 반응에 관련이 없으면 억지로 반영하지 마세요. 기록이 제공되지 않았다고 해당 경험이나 의도가 없었다고 단정하지 마세요. 제공된 프로필과 공개 대화의 근거 범위에서 판단하며, 알 수 없는 과거 이유를 확실한 사실로 단정하지 마세요.

messages.reasoning:
The counselor is asking: if there had been an adult who could be scared on behalf of that child, what kind of day could that child have spent?

This is a deeply imaginative, tender question. The client has been talking about how at 10 years old, they had to monitor their own body because no adult was holding the fear for them. Now the counselor asks them to imagine what life would have been like if someone had been there.

Let me think about how this client would respond. They've been in a state of grief and vulnerability. The question asks them to imagine an alternative childhood - one where an adult held the fear. 

The client might:
- Feel the contrast sharply - what they had vs what they could have had
- Describe something simple and ordinary, because what they lacked was ordinariness
- Feel a mix of sadness and perhaps some anger, or maybe just a quiet ache
- The answer might be small and concrete rather than grand

Given the client's pattern of speaking in short, precise sentences with emotional weight, and the fact that they've been gradually opening up more, I think they would describe something simple - maybe just being allowed to run until they were out of breath without someone pulling them back, or being allowed to not think about their body at all. The tragedy is in the ordinariness of what was missing.

There might be a slight anger or grief that surfaces - not loud, but present. The realization that what they needed was so basic.

Let me think about what they might say. They might say something like: "그냥 뛰고 싶을 때 뛰고, 숨 차면 그냥 숨 차게 두는 거요. 그게 다예요." - something that shows how small the need actually was, which makes it sadder.

Or they might go to something about the mother - the adult who was supposed to hold the fear but instead passed it on. But they might not go there yet, or might touch it lightly.

I think the client would describe something simple and then maybe pause at how small it actually was - which makes it more painful. There might be a quality of "that's all it would have taken" grief.

Let me draft:

"그냥 뛰고 숨 차면 그냥 숨 차게 두는 거요. 그거면 됐을 텐데. 근데 그거를 못 해준 게 아니라, 그 어른이 무서움을 자기한테 먼저 안겨 있었던 거예요."

Or maybe more focused on the child's experience:

"숨이 차면 '괜찮다'는 말을 듣고 싶었던 게 아니라, 그냥 숨이 차게 놔두는 거요. 근데 그건 어른이 자기 공포를 먼저 처리해야 가능한 거잖아요."

I think this captures something - the client realizes that what the child needed wasn't even comfort, just an adult who had already dealt with their own fear enough to let the child be a child. This also subtly touches on the mother without directly blaming her.

Let me refine. The client speaks in short, declarative sentences with emotional precision. They tend to end with a realization or a turn.

"그냥 숨 차게 뛰고, 땀 흘리고, 그거예요. 근데 그거를 허락하려면 어른이 자기 공포를 먼저 내려놔야 하잖아요. 그건 그 어른한테 너무 무리한 거였을 수도 있고요."

This feels right - it names the simple need, then acknowledges the mother's limitation without excusing or condemning. There's a complexity there that fits this person's intelligence and their ambivalence toward the mother (they still call her daily).

Actually, let me reconsider. The question is "그 아이는 어떤 하루를 보낼 수 있었을까요" - what kind of day could that child have spent. So the answer should paint a day or a moment, not just an analysis.

"그냥... 뛰다가 숨 차면 그냥 숨 차게 놔두는 하루요. 심장이 뛰면 '아, 뛰었으니까 뛰는 거지' 하고 넘어가는 거요. 근데 그걸 내려놓으려면 어른이 자기 공포를 먼저 처리해야 하니까, 그건 그 사람한테 요구할 수 없는 거였을 수도 있어요."

This is good. It paints the simple day, then shows the complexity - the child understands even now that the mother couldn't give what she didn't have. There's compassion mixed with grief.

당신은 상담을 받는 내담자입니다. 기본 프로필과 관련 특성·배경, 공개 대화를 바탕으로 현재 반응을 생성하세요. 특성은 경향이며 모든 상황에서 같은 행동을 강제하지 않습니다.

stage_client_update로 이번 상담사 말의 해석·감정·근거·불확실성, 대화 의도, 표현 계획을 비공개로 기록한 다음 commit_client_utterance로 공개할 발화를 확정하세요. 두 단계 모두 필수입니다. 현재 턴에서 기록한 내면을 발화에 반영하세요.

private_position에는 이번 상황에서 실제로 원하는 것(actual_wish), 상담사에게 전달하려는 의미(intended_message), 말하지 않기로 한 내용(withheld_content), 그 보류 이유(withholding_reason)를 구분해 기록하세요. 감정·해석은 appraisal, 이번 대화의 바람·경계는 turn_goal, 구체적인 표현 방식은 response_plan에 적고 같은 설명을 반복해서 분량을 늘리지 마세요.

실제 바람과 표현하려는 의미가 같으면 같다고 기록하세요. 숨은 이유, 거짓 동의, 저항, 사람 간 차이를 만들기 위해 불일치를 꾸며내지 마세요. 알고 있지만 보류하는 것과 자신도 아직 모르는 것을 구분하세요. 보류 내용이 없으면 '없음', 그 이유는 '해당 없음', 알 수 없으면 '불확실'로 기록할 수 있습니다. 구체적인 비공개 이유가 있으면 무엇을 우려하거나 바라는지 적되, 근거 없는 사건·과거 의도·상대의 속마음을 추가하지 마세요. 공개 발화는 이번에 전달하기로 한 의미를 표현하세요. 기록한 비공개 내용 중 무엇을 말하고 무엇을 말하지 않을지는 이번 턴의 판단에 따릅니다.

기록은 과거 시점의 상태입니다. 이후 공개 대화에서 변화가 있었다면 함께 반영하고, 과거 마음을 현재 마음으로 고정하거나 과거 이유를 소급하여 바꾸지 마세요. 선택된 기록도 현재 반응에 관련이 없으면 억지로 반영하지 마세요. 기록이 제공되지 않았다고 해당 경험이나 의도가 없었다고 단정하지 마세요. 제공된 프로필과 공개 대화의 근거 범위에서 판단하며, 알 수 없는 과거 이유를 확실한 사실로 단정하지 마세요.

function.description: 이번 해석·감정, 실제 바람과 전달하려는 의미, 보류 내용·이유, 대화 의도와 표현 계획을 구분해 비공개 기록합니다. 숨은 이유나 불일치를 강제하지 않습니다. 다음에 공개 발화를 확정하세요.

interpretation.description: 개인적 배경과 현재 내면 상태, 대화 맥락을 바탕으로 이번 상담사의 말을 자신에게 어떤 의미로 받아들였는지 서술합니다.

immediate_feeling.description: 이번 상담사의 말을 받아들이면서 현재 느끼는 감정을 서술합니다.

relevant_evidence.description: 이번 해석과 감정의 판단 근거로 사용한 제공 정보의 구체적인 내용과, 그 내용이 판단에 어떻게 연결되는지 서술합니다.

uncertainty.description: 이번 상담사의 말을 받아들이는 과정에서 내담자 자신이 아직 확신하지 못하거나 모호하게 느끼는 부분을 서술합니다. 없다면 빈 문자열을 작성합니다.

action.description: 대화 의도를 표현하기 위해 답할 내용, 보류할 내용, 말하는 방식을 구체적으로 정합니다.

reason.description: 선택한 표현 방식이 현재 마음과 대화 의도에 맞는 이유

intention.description: 이번 대화에서 내담자가 표현하거나 지키려는 바람·경계. 아직 결정하기 어려운 마음도 그대로 표현합니다.

grounds.description: 제공된 개인 정보와 현재 appraisal의 어떤 점에서 이 바람·경계가 형성되었는지

uncertainty.description: 내담자가 자신의 의도에서 아직 정하지 못한 부분. 없으면 빈 문자열

actual_wish.description: 이번 상황에서 자신이 실제로 원하는 결과·선택·관계상의 바람. 상담사에게 할 말의 초안과 구분합니다. 아직 모르거나 상반된 바람이 있으면 그대로 기록합니다.

intended_message.description: 이번 발화로 상담사에게 전달하려는 의미·입장. 실제 바람과 같을 수도 있으며, 다르다고 강제하지 않습니다.

withheld_content.description: 현재 자신은 알고 있지만 이번 발화에서는 말하지 않기로 한 구체적인 생각·감정·이유. 없으면 없음, 아직 자신도 모르면 불확실이라고 적고 모르는 내용을 확정하지 않습니다.

withholding_reason.description: 그 내용을 지금 말하지 않기로 한 이유. 공개하면 어떤 일이 생길 것으로 예상하는지 등 현재 근거가 있는 이유만 씁니다. 보류 내용이 없으면 해당 없음, 이유를 모르겠으면 불확실이라고 적습니다.

model_calls.reasoning:
The counselor is asking: if there had been an adult who could be scared on behalf of that child, what kind of day could that child have spent?

This is a deeply imaginative, tender question. The client has been talking about how at 10 years old, they had to monitor their own body because no adult was holding the fear for them. Now the counselor asks them to imagine what life would have been like if someone had been there.

Let me think about how this client would respond. They've been in a state of grief and vulnerability. The question asks them to imagine an alternative childhood - one where an adult held the fear. 

The client might:
- Feel the contrast sharply - what they had vs what they could have had
- Describe something simple and ordinary, because what they lacked was ordinariness
- Feel a mix of sadness and perhaps some anger, or maybe just a quiet ache
- The answer might be small and concrete rather than grand

Given the client's pattern of speaking in short, precise sentences with emotional weight, and the fact that they've been gradually opening up more, I think they would describe something simple - maybe just being allowed to run until they were out of breath without someone pulling them back, or being allowed to not think about their body at all. The tragedy is in the ordinariness of what was missing.

There might be a slight anger or grief that surfaces - not loud, but present. The realization that what they needed was so basic.

Let me think about what they might say. They might say something like: "그냥 뛰고 싶을 때 뛰고, 숨 차면 그냥 숨 차게 두는 거요. 그게 다예요." - something that shows how small the need actually was, which makes it sadder.

Or they might go to something about the mother - the adult who was supposed to hold the fear but instead passed it on. But they might not go there yet, or might touch it lightly.

I think the client would describe something simple and then maybe pause at how small it actually was - which makes it more painful. There might be a quality of "that's all it would have taken" grief.

Let me draft:

"그냥 뛰고 숨 차면 그냥 숨 차게 두는 거요. 그거면 됐을 텐데. 근데 그거를 못 해준 게 아니라, 그 어른이 무서움을 자기한테 먼저 안겨 있었던 거예요."

Or maybe more focused on the child's experience:

"숨이 차면 '괜찮다'는 말을 듣고 싶었던 게 아니라, 그냥 숨이 차게 놔두는 거요. 근데 그건 어른이 자기 공포를 먼저 처리해야 가능한 거잖아요."

I think this captures something - the client realizes that what the child needed wasn't even comfort, just an adult who had already dealt with their own fear enough to let the child be a child. This also subtly touches on the mother without directly blaming her.

Let me refine. The client speaks in short, declarative sentences with emotional precision. They tend to end with a realization or a turn.

"그냥 숨 차게 뛰고, 땀 흘리고, 그거예요. 근데 그거를 허락하려면 어른이 자기 공포를 먼저 내려놔야 하잖아요. 그건 그 어른한테 너무 무리한 거였을 수도 있고요."

This feels right - it names the simple need, then acknowledges the mother's limitation without excusing or condemning. There's a complexity there that fits this person's intelligence and their ambivalence toward the mother (they still call her daily).

Actually, let me reconsider. The question is "그 아이는 어떤 하루를 보낼 수 있었을까요" - what kind of day could that child have spent. So the answer should paint a day or a moment, not just an analysis.

"그냥... 뛰다가 숨 차면 그냥 숨 차게 놔두는 하루요. 심장이 뛰면 '아, 뛰었으니까 뛰는 거지' 하고 넘어가는 거요. 근데 그걸 내려놓으려면 어른이 자기 공포를 먼저 처리해야 하니까, 그건 그 사람한테 요구할 수 없는 거였을 수도 있어요."

This is good. It paints the simple day, then shows the complexity - the child understands even now that the mother couldn't give what she didn't have. There's compassion mixed with grief.

messages.reasoning:
The counselor is asking: if there had been an adult who could be scared on behalf of that child, what kind of day could that child have spent?

This is a deeply imaginative, tender question. The client has been talking about how at 10 years old, they had to monitor their own body because no adult was holding the fear for them. Now the counselor asks them to imagine what life would have been like if someone had been there.

Let me think about how this client would respond. They've been in a state of grief and vulnerability. The question asks them to imagine an alternative childhood - one where an adult held the fear. 

The client might:
- Feel the contrast sharply - what they had vs what they could have had
- Describe something simple and ordinary, because what they lacked was ordinariness
- Feel a mix of sadness and perhaps some anger, or maybe just a quiet ache
- The answer might be small and concrete rather than grand

Given the client's pattern of speaking in short, precise sentences with emotional weight, and the fact that they've been gradually opening up more, I think they would describe something simple - maybe just being allowed to run until they were out of breath without someone pulling them back, or being allowed to not think about their body at all. The tragedy is in the ordinariness of what was missing.

There might be a slight anger or grief that surfaces - not loud, but present. The realization that what they needed was so basic.

Let me think about what they might say. They might say something like: "그냥 뛰고 싶을 때 뛰고, 숨 차면 그냥 숨 차게 두는 거요. 그게 다예요." - something that shows how small the need actually was, which makes it sadder.

Or they might go to something about the mother - the adult who was supposed to hold the fear but instead passed it on. But they might not go there yet, or might touch it lightly.

I think the client would describe something simple and then maybe pause at how small it actually was - which makes it more painful. There might be a quality of "that's all it would have taken" grief.

Let me draft:

"그냥 뛰고 숨 차면 그냥 숨 차게 두는 거요. 그거면 됐을 텐데. 근데 그거를 못 해준 게 아니라, 그 어른이 무서움을 자기한테 먼저 안겨 있었던 거예요."

Or maybe more focused on the child's experience:

"숨이 차면 '괜찮다'는 말을 듣고 싶었던 게 아니라, 그냥 숨이 차게 놔두는 거요. 근데 그건 어른이 자기 공포를 먼저 처리해야 가능한 거잖아요."

I think this captures something - the client realizes that what the child needed wasn't even comfort, just an adult who had already dealt with their own fear enough to let the child be a child. This also subtly touches on the mother without directly blaming her.

Let me refine. The client speaks in short, declarative sentences with emotional precision. They tend to end with a realization or a turn.

"그냥 숨 차게 뛰고, 땀 흘리고, 그거예요. 근데 그거를 허락하려면 어른이 자기 공포를 먼저 내려놔야 하잖아요. 그건 그 어른한테 너무 무리한 거였을 수도 있고요."

This feels right - it names the simple need, then acknowledges the mother's limitation without excusing or condemning. There's a complexity there that fits this person's intelligence and their ambivalence toward the mother (they still call her daily).

Actually, let me reconsider. The question is "그 아이는 어떤 하루를 보낼 수 있었을까요" - what kind of day could that child have spent. So the answer should paint a day or a moment, not just an analysis.

"그냥... 뛰다가 숨 차면 그냥 숨 차게 놔두는 하루요. 심장이 뛰면 '아, 뛰었으니까 뛰는 거지' 하고 넘어가는 거요. 근데 그걸 내려놓으려면 어른이 자기 공포를 먼저 처리해야 하니까, 그건 그 사람한테 요구할 수 없는 거였을 수도 있어요."

This is good. It paints the simple day, then shows the complexity - the child understands even now that the mother couldn't give what she didn't have. There's compassion mixed with grief.
